Kennedy International Airport (JFK) are both located in Queens, New York City. While the straight-line distance between them is short, the actual transfer time can vary widely depending on traffic, time of day, and transportation choice. The airports are roughly 10 to 13 miles apart, but real-world travel typically takes 30 to 90+ minutes by road. For travelers with tight connections, choosing the right transfer method matters more than the distance itself. LGA to JFK quick distance and transfer overview Item Details Distance between airports About 10 to 13 miles Typical driving time 30 to 90+ minutes Public transportation time 60 to 100+ minutes Fastest scheduled air segment Manhattan helicopter flight about 5 minutes Best option for tight connections Helicopter via Manhattan plus short car transfer Exact distance between LaGuardia and JFK The shortest driving distance between LaGuardia Airport and JFK Airport is typically about 11 miles, though routes may extend to around 13 miles depending on traffic patterns and road selection. Both airports are in Queens but are not directly connected by a single fast transit corridor. Heavy congestion on the Grand Central Parkway, Van Wyck Expressway, and surrounding roads often increases travel time significantly. Because of this, the distance alone does not determine how long your transfer will take. Traffic reliability is usually the deciding factor. Transportation options between LGA and JFK Travelers comparing their options for how to get from JFK to LaGuardia Airport can choose from several transfer methods depending on budget, luggage, and schedule flexibility. Taxi or rideshare When planning a JFK to LGA transfer, taxis and services like Uber or Lyft offer door-to-door routing between the airports. Typical travel time: 30 to 75+ minutes Estimated cost: $35 to $70 depending on traffic and demand Best for: convenience and direct routing Traffic congestion is the biggest variable with this option, particularly during weekday rush hours. Shuttle services Shared airport shuttle providers operate transfers between LGA and JFK. Typical travel time: 60 to 90 minutes Estimated cost: $15 to $25 per person Best for: budget-conscious travelers with flexible schedules Because these vehicles make multiple stops, they are slower than taxis. Public transportation Public transit is the cheapest method but also the most complex. A typical route involves: Bus from LaGuardia to a subway station Subway toward Queens or Brooklyn AirTrain connection into JFK Typical travel time: 75 to 100+ minutes Estimated cost: about $11 total Best for: travelers with light luggage and plenty of time This option is not ideal for tight flight connections. Can you transfer between LGA and JFK using a helicopter? Yes, through a Manhattan helicopter connection. Scheduled helicopter airport transfers operate between Manhattan and JFK. Travelers transferring between LaGuardia and JFK can combine: A short ground transfer between LGA and Manhattan, similar to common routes for getting to Manhattan from JFK, Newark, or LaGuardia A scheduled helicopter flight between Manhattan and JFK The helicopter segment itself takes about 5 minutes of flight time, allowing travelers to bypass the most congested parts of New York City road traffic. While this is not a direct airport-to-airport helicopter route, it is often the most time-predictable transfer strategy available for urgent connections or international departures. Best time of day to travel between LGA and JFK Traffic patterns strongly affect transfer times. Generally smoother travel windows: Early morning between 5 a.m. and 7 a.m. Late evening after 9 p.m. Peak congestion periods to avoid when possible: Weekday mornings from 7 a.m. to 10 a.m. Weekday evenings from 4 p.m. to 7 p.m. If you must travel during these peak periods and have a tight connection, using a scheduled air segment for part of the journey can significantly improve timing reliability. Tips for transferring between LaGuardia and JFK Allow at least 2 to 3 hours for airport transfers when possible Always factor in baggage collection time Check real-time traffic conditions before leaving Pre-book transportation whenever possible Choose the most predictable option if you have an international departure Even though the airports are geographically close, road delays can quickly create missed connections without proper planning, which is why understanding how to get to LaGuardia Airport in advance can help prevent unnecessary stress. FAQs about the distance between LaGuardia and JFK How far is LaGuardia Airport from JFK Airport? The airports are about 10 to 13 miles apart, depending on the driving route. How long does it take to travel between LGA and JFK? Travel time usually ranges from 30 minutes to over 90 minutes, depending on traffic and transportation method. What is the fastest way to transfer between the airports? For travelers researching the best way to get to Manhattan from airport, combining a scheduled Manhattan helicopter flight with a short car transfer often provides the most reliable timing. Can I take public transportation between the airports? Yes. Public transit options exist, but they typically require multiple transfers and take 75 minutes or longer. Should I schedule extra time for airport transfers? Yes. Because traffic in Queens can be unpredictable, travelers should always allow extra buffer time when transferring between LGA and JFK. Final summary Although LaGuardia and JFK are only about a dozen miles apart, the real challenge is navigating New York City traffic. Ground transfers can vary widely in duration, making planning essential. For budget travelers, public transportation and shared shuttles remain viable options. For those prioritizing speed, reliability, and connection security, combining scheduled air transfer with a short ground segment can provide the most predictable journey between the two airports.
